issue_context.title: SharedIndexInformers can miss create notifications
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
I did a review of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache and found out a case where a SharedIndexInformer can miss a notification. Follows an example scenario where this could happen.

1) A SharedIndexInformer is running, and its reflector is WATCHing.
2) A delete notification for an API object _X_ with namespaced name _N1_ and UID _U1_ which was in the informer's cache is received.
3) The reflector [invokes the store's Delete method](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L395-L399) on _X_; the relevant store is a DeltaFIFO and its Delete method is [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L191).
4) The DeltaFIFO's Delete method invokes [queueActionLocked](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L219), which [enqueues _N1_ in the DeltaFIFO's queue and adds a delta of type deleted to the map from objects IDs (namespaced names) to deltas](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L320-L328).

Notice that the store of the reflector, i.e., the DeltaFIFO, is NOT the SharedIndexInformer's store/cache: [the SharedIndexInformer extracts object deltas from the DeltaFIFO and modifies its cache accordingly](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L448-L477). Assume that BEFORE _X_'s deletion is popped from the DeltaFIFO and applied to the informer's cache, the following sequence of events take place:

5) The WATCH is interrupted because of a network partition.
6) While the reflector is not watching, a new API object _Y_ with namespaced name _N1_ (same as _X_) and UID _U2_ is created.
7) The partition disappears and the reflector does a relist against the API server; there's a "hole" between the last watch notification and the list results; assume _Y_ is in the LIST results.
8) The reflector will load the LIST results in the store/DeltaFIFO with [syncWith](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L240) which in turn calls the DeltaFIFO's [replace](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L340) method. The DeltaFIFO's replace method attempts to add to the DeltaFIFO a delta of type `Sync` for every object in the LIST results: when processing _Y_ it will [invoke queueActionLocked](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L456-L462) which should [create a delta of type `Sync` for  Y and add it to the DeltaFIFO](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L320-L328). But `queueActionLocked` won't enqueue Y's delta, because it enqueues deltas of type `Sync` only if there's not already a delta of type `Deleted` for the given object ID as the last delta for that object ID (see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L313-L318) and [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L298-L303)), to avoid recreating a deleted object during a periodic resync triggered by the SharedIndexInformer resync period. Object IDs are namespaced names,  and remember that the last delta for Y's namespaced name in the DeltaFIFO is _X_'s deletion. The consequence is that _Y_'s creation delta is not added to the DeltaFIFO: Y is not added to the SharedIndexInformer's cache and its creation notification handler does not execute. The SharedIndexInformer missed Y's creation. 

**What you expected to happen**:
I expected SharedIndexInformers to get all notifications from the API server.

**Anything else we need to know?**
Missed notifications should be rare: for them to occur a `Delete` delta must stay in the DeltaFIFO without being processed for long enough for a new List against the API server to be completed. Also, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83520 touches the reflector code that handles list and watches, and it might introduce changes relevant to this bug.

**Proposed solution**:
There's a straightforward fix: get rid of the check that skips enqueuing of a `Sync` delta for object ID _X_ if the last delta added to the DeltaFIFO (and still in it) for _X_  is of type  `Delete`;  [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L313-L318) is the code to remove. Notice that such check applies to deltas of type `Sync` only. `Sync` deltas are triggered only by relists and periodic resyncs. In the case of relists the check is harmful as it's the cause of this bug. In the case of periodic resyncs, that check is useless because it will either evaluate to `false` or not execute; in fact, during a period resync, [processing of an object with ID _X_ stops if there's already a delta for _X_ in the DeltaFIFO](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L560-L562) and this condition is checked before the check that would be removed, OTOH, if this condition is true and processing goes on the check that would be removed can only evaluate to `false` (hence the delta for _X_ is enqueued). If this solution has consensus I'd be happy to open a PR.

It's a little hard to reason about what this sync event should be when we know that relists can currently time-travel backwards.

Edit: it looks like shared informer code will [turn the Sync event into an Added event](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L456-L468) if it follows a delete event.

I was [just asking about this very situation](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0EG7JC6T/p1571054208147900) this morning in the "sig-api-machinery" channel of the "Kubernetes" Slack team. My reading of the code had me expecting that I'd get a _delete_ followed by an _add_.

> I was [just asking about this very situation](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0EG7JC6T/p1571054208147900) this morning in the "sig-api-machinery" channel of the "Kubernetes" Slack team. My reading of the code had me expecting that I'd get a _delete_ followed by an _add_.

This issue is specifically focused on how a queued delete event (typically via directly observing a delete watch event or via absence in a relist/replace) followed by an observed add (via presence in a relist) is handled by DeltaFIFO.

@seh, your question is slightly broader/different, and has multiple facets:
1. Are UID changes considered when handling reflector object add/delete/update events? They are not; if an object is deleted and recreated between the reflector dropping a watch and relisting, the reflector will enqueue an Sync event with the object with the new uid (which the shared informer will turn into an Update event)
2. Are delete/add events is actively compressed into an update event? I don't think so, but it's been a while since I've traipsed through reflector/fifo code, so I'm not positive (and since the Update with a new uid can occur from scenario 1, informer clients have to be prepared for uid to change on update anyway)
@seh Listeners need to handle Sync too. And the only two in-tree users of NewDeltaFIFO are cache/controller.go and cache/shared_informer.go and they look like they correctly handle Sync.

>     2\. Are delete/add events is actively compressed into an update event? I don't think so, but it's been a while since I've traipsed through reflector/fifo code, so I'm not positive (and since the Update with a new uid can occur from scenario 1, informer clients have to be prepared for uid to change on update anyway)

Edit: @liggitt yep you're right, I was looking at slightly older code.

> IMHO it's correct that Deletes don't get compressed, eg that Delete + Add is not compressed into Update or something like that.

I agree, though that specific example **can** happen naturally if it occurs in a window while the reflector isn't getting watch events.

> that specific example **can** happen naturally if it occurs in a window while the reflector isn't getting watch events.

exactly (both namespace and name are part of the cache key, uid is not)

As noted in Slack, there is now careful commentary in https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/tools/cache/shared_informer.go about what is promised.  There is no promise that a delete followed by an add is delivered as two notifications; it is allowed to be delivered as one update notification.

review_comments:
We should ignore sync events *if the UID hasn't changed* and not ignore them *if it has changed*.

The bug this is talking about is when sync resurrected an object that was already deleted, and then it lived on forever as a zombie.

Folks in other comments are saying that there's no race, but I would expect the queue getting drained depends on the consumer, but the sync event depends on the producer.

In theory, if we've observed the deletion event, we shouldn't be able to then see the object in a relist, but that depends on apiserver & etcd getting things exactly right. Which they should, nowadays. Maybe the best response to this is to detect it and panic, to make sure we get a bug report if it happens.

Separate protections (and covering unit tests) were already added for the resync case. If a relist time travels back in time, it will replay history, but that is a separate bigger issue and applies to more than just the initial sync event queued up (and from the reflector's perspective, the subsequent watch will catch up after replaying history)

As long as that condition results in a panic (we REALLY need to know if it happens) now, I'm good. I'm pretty sure this condition is why the code is like it is. Maybe it was always just a theoretical problem.

The original code combined replace and resync flows. This protection was added in as an attempt to fix the resync issue, which introduced a bug in the relist flow, and didn't completely solve the resync issue (hence the follow up separation and resync-specific fix in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/32125, which is still present/effective)

> As long as that condition results in a panic (we REALLY need to know if it happens) now, I'm good

I  don't think it's DeltaFIFOs job to do that. Accepting a list of items in Replace, setting them in the store, and not propagating a Sync event for one seems like a pretty contained bug to me.

Also, DeltaFIFO would only be able to recognize that scenario if the Deleted event hadn't been popped yet, so it's not like it would provide great protection from that condition. For every time travel caught that way, it would be more likely the Deleted event had already been popped and a new sync event would be happily delivered. There's also a whole class of time-travel bugs that that wouldn't catch (sync followed by updates from the past with no delete involved)

/hold

`Controller should ignore "Sync" event on deleted objects. When controller receives 'object deleted' event from etcd and at the same time it starts periodic sync, "Sync" event can be enqueued after "Delete" event. Processing "Deleted" event, controller removes the object from its cache. It should not create the object there when processing "Sync" event after that.`
